title: Nuclear Thermal Propulsion
description: A chemical rocket's exhaust is heavy water vapour; a nuclear thermal rocket heats pure hydrogen in a reactor instead. The exhaust speed goes as the square root of temperature over molar mass, and hydrogen's molar mass is 2 against steam's 18, so at a lower temperature it still leaves twice as fast. NERVA ran on the test stand in the 1960s at about 900 seconds of specific impulse. Unlocks the Nuclear Thermal Core.

puzzle.goal: A gas of ratio of specific heats γ and molar mass M leaves a chamber at temperature T through an ideal nozzle into vacuum. Write its exhaust speed ve, with R the gas constant.
puzzle.name: Exhaust speed
puzzle.form: sqrt ( 2 * γ / ( γ - 1 ) * R * T / M )
puzzle.expr: sqrt ( 2 * g / ( g - 1 ) * R * T / M )
puzzle.ask: Find ve in m/s for hydrogen (γ = 1.4, M = 0.002 kg/mol) at T = @{T} K, R = 8.314.
puzzle.method: The gas's enthalpy cp·T, all of it turned into motion: ve² = 2·cp·T, with cp = γR/((γ − 1)M).
